meta.description: A presence layer for glasses wearers: see who nearby is open to a conversation, and who wants quiet. Privacy-first, ephemeral, opt-in.
meta.title_home: Urban Inversion — see who's open to a conversation
footer.line: No accounts. No tracking. Positions live only briefly in server memory and never leave it.
home.lede_a: Urban Inversion is a presence layer for glasses wearers. As you walk, your glasses quietly show who nearby is
home.lede_b: — so approaching someone is welcome, and giving someone space is easy.
home.pills_note: You choose your state moment to moment. Go invisible and the app disconnects completely — the server holds nothing about you at all.
home.why_p: Cities spent a decade designing people into bubbles — screens, buds, blank stares. This inverts the signal: the same wearable technology that sealed us off becomes a small, consent-based beacon for the analog thing it replaced: a chat with whoever happens to be there.
home.privacy_p_a: No accounts, no names, no faces, no camera use. Your position exists only in server memory for a few seconds and is shared with nobody — others see only a rough direction and distance category, and only while you are visible yourself.
home.privacy_link: Exactly how it works, in detail.
home.start_p_a: The experience runs in the browser of display glasses (currently the Ray-Ban Display web-app runtime) at
home.start_p_b: — added once via the Meta AI app in Developer Mode, then it's just a URL. Start on the
how.title: How it works
how.states_quiet: you're visible with a clear "please don't approach".
how.states_observer: you see only counts — never individuals — and are never visible.
how.states_invisible: disconnects everything: no socket, no server state.
how.see_p: While walking, open people appear as a soft green marker and quiet people as a dim one — at a glanceable direction and distance category like "about 20–30 m, slightly left". That resolution is deliberate: it's enough to decide whether to say hello, and too coarse to follow anyone. People outside your narrow field of view appear as edge indicators. Text is kept to a minimum; this is a HUD, not a feed.
how.mutual_p: You only ever see individual markers while you are yourself visible (Open or Quiet). There is no way to watch open people while staying unseen — the silent-observer loophole is closed by design. Observers get aggregate counts only, and so does anyone whose location source is too imprecise that moment.
how.compass_p: Glasses have no reliable compass, so the display aligns to the real world by walking: after a few straight steps the app compares how far you moved per your GPS track versus your tracked head movement and locks the orientation. Until then it tells you plainly: "alignment low — walk straight for a few seconds."
how.device_p: The experience is a plain web app at /xr on this site. On Ray-Ban Display glasses you add it once via the Meta AI app in Developer Mode (URL or QR code) — no store, no install. Developers can run the same build on a laptop with the IWER emulator and a simulated walker.
privacy.title: Privacy & safety
privacy.lede: This page describes what the running code actually does — not an aspiration. It tracks the implementation, and changes when the code does.
privacy.short_p: No accounts, no names, no faces, no camera use, no third-party trackers or analytics. Your precise position exists only in server memory, for at most half a minute, and is never sent to another user — others see only a direction category, a distance category, and a rotating anonymous handle. Going invisible disconnects you entirely: the server then holds nothing about you at all.
privacy.identity_p: Each session, your browser generates a fresh cryptographic key pair (did:key, P-256) and discards it afterward. It signs your messages so nobody can forge or tamper with them. It is not an identity: there is no profile, no login, and no way to link one session to the next. One anti-abuse mechanism runs at session start — a Cloudflare Turnstile challenge on the Enter page — plus rate limits per connection and per network (networks are counted only as short-lived salted hashes, never stored as addresses).
privacy.location_p: While active you send position updates several times a minute. They live only in a server-side Durable Object's memory with a 30-second expiry — never in a database, never in logs, never in backups. The glasses have no GPS; the phone they're paired with supplies location through the operating system. If the reported accuracy is too coarse for individual markers, you are not rejected — you simply see counts instead of people, and the interface says so.
privacy.others_h: What other people can see about you
privacy.others_p: When you are Open or Quiet, nearby visible users see: a direction bucket (45°), a distance bucket (10 m), your state, and an opaque handle that rotates every 5 minutes. Never your coordinates, never your key, never anything stable across sessions. You only appear to people who are themselves visible — there is no silent observation. Observers see aggregate counts only. Any user can block you for their session, and you them.
privacy.stats_p: We keep one database table: counts of Open/Quiet/Observer users per 15-minute window per coarse area (~20 km cell). Rows are written only when an area has at least 5 people in the window after combining small areas — below that, nothing is stored at all. No identifiers, no positions, no finer time resolution exists anywhere in storage.
privacy.limit_1: A determined person moving physically while visible to you could, over minutes, estimate a visible person's rough location from repeated bearing/distance categories. Quantization, per-pair noise, movement plausibility checks and mutual visibility raise the cost — they cannot eliminate it. The product's own display is the alarm: a visible marker closing in on you is exactly what you see.
privacy.limit_2: Operating any website means Cloudflare transiently processes IP addresses and request metadata. We do not persist them or use them for analytics.
privacy.limit_3: Functional state (your consent and the anti-abuse token) lives in the tab's session storage and disappears when the tab does.
privacy.controls_p_a: State toggle (Open / Quiet / Observer / Invisible) is one gesture away at all times. Invisible means zero server-side state, by construction and by test. Questions:
enter.title: Before you enter
enter.lede: One explicit opt-in, one quick human check — then the glasses take over.
enter.consent_a: I understand that while I am Open or Quiet, people nearby can see an anonymous, coarse indication of my direction and state — never my name, face, or exact location — and that I can go invisible at any time. See

pair.title: Pair a phone
pair.lede: This page is a stub. Phone pairing is intentionally not implemented in v1.
pair.why_p: Ray-Ban Display glasses pair with a phone at the operating-system level, and the glasses' web runtime exposes that phone-sourced location to web apps directly. The XR client reads it through its location provider, so there is nothing to pair in-app.
pair.what_p: If on-device measurements ever show the runtime's location is unusable, this page becomes the companion flow: a short-lived pairing code shown in XR, entered here on the phone, after which the phone streams GPS and compass into your session over the same presence infrastructure. The client-side interface for that provider already exists in the code as a documented stub.
